Jim Morrison and Jimmy Chin Rappel Down West Hollywood Building to Promote ‘Everest: The Other Side’

02 Nov 2026, 08:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Entertainment Desk · Source: deadline.com

A high‑rise promotional stunt

On Friday evening, Olympic‑medalist filmmaker Jimmy Chin and extreme‑sports athlete Jim Morrison climbed to the roof of a 12‑story building on the Sunset Strip in West Hollywood, California. From there they rappelled down the façade, using the same rope system they would employ on a mountain face. The descent was captured on video and posted alongside the film’s advertising billboard that dominates the building’s side.

  • Location: 12‑story commercial building, Sunset Strip, West Hollywood, CA
  • Purpose: To draw attention to the National Geographic documentary *Everest: The Other Side* ahead of its wide theatrical release on Dec. 1, 2026 (551 theaters, including IMAX)
  • Visual: The billboard features the film’s title and a dramatic image of Morrison on the north side of Everest.

Morrison, with his skis strapped to his back, said the rappel was “definitely too steep” but recalled the feeling of looking down a line on Everest with Chin by his side. He added that the stunt was a “pinch‑me moment,” not a dangerous one for him.

About the documentary

*Everest: The Other Side* is directed by Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi, the Oscar‑winning team behind *Free Solo*. The film chronicles Morrison’s historic 2021 ascent of the north face of Mount Everest and his subsequent ski descent of the Hornbein Couloir – the first ever ski run down that side of the mountain.

  • Premiere circuit: Venice Film Festival (world premiere), followed by Telluride and Toronto.
  • Release strategy: Limited theatrical run in December, then a debut on HBO later in the year.
  • Key themes: Adventure, loss, and the drive to honor a fallen partner.

The personal backstory

Morrison’s partner, elite ski‑mountaineer Hilaree Nelson, died in an avalanche on Manaslu in September 2022 while the pair were on a climbing expedition. Chin confirmed that he stayed in close contact with Morrison throughout the grieving period and that the documentary’s narrative shifted to include how Morrison coped with the tragedy and chose to complete the Everest goal they had shared.

> “We were in communication with Jim the whole time,” Chin said during a Q&A at the Academy Museum screening.

Morrison described the emotional impact of watching the finished film with friends and crew: “When it ended, I went up to Jimmy and we were both crying. I told him, ‘I lived it, Jimmy. I lived all of it.’”

Practical implications and verification

  • How to verify the stunt: The video of the rappel is available on the film’s official YouTube channel and was referenced in the Deadline article dated Oct 30, 2026. The building’s billboard can be seen in street‑level photos posted by local news outlets.
  • Where to find the documentary: Check the National Geographic website, HBO’s upcoming releases page, or the film’s official social‑media accounts for the exact release dates and theater listings.
  • Fact‑checking tips: Cross‑reference the claim that the film opened in 551 theaters with box‑office tracking sites (e.g., Box Office Mojo) and confirm the IMAX locations through the IMAX website.

Audience takeaways

The rappel serves as a visual metaphor for the steep challenges Morrison faces on the mountain and in life. By turning a promotional event into a live‑action demonstration of rope work, Chin and Morrison reinforce the documentary’s core message: pushing limits, honoring loss, and continuing the pursuit of seemingly impossible goals.
